definitions.meaning: To take, lay hold of, take captive

source_text: ge-hæftnan, -hæftnian; p. ede, ade; pp. ed, ad To take, lay hold of, take captive; comprehend&e-short;re, capt&i-long;v&a-long;re :-- Ðú me gehæftnedest [gehæft&dash-uncertain;nadest, Exon. 98 a; Th. 368; 29] thou didst take me captive, Soul Kmbl. 63; Seel. 32. Sý éhtende oððe éhte feónd míne sáwle and gehæftnige hí oððe gegrípe hí pers&e-short;qu&a-long;tur in&i-short;m&i-long;cus an&i-short;mam meam et comprehendat, Ps. Lamb. 7, 6. Ða ðe ǽr gehæftnede wǽron who before were held cap&dash-uncertain;tive, Blickl. Homl. 87, 7 : 89, 29.
